\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Linear form on the Boolean cube]
\lean{FABL.linearForm}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p127-b004}
\label{FABL.linearForm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.signValue}
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}$ and let $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The linear
form with coefficients $a_i$ evaluated at $x$ is $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Centered square of a linear form]
\lean{FABL.centeredLinearSquare}
\label{FABL.centeredLinearSquare}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.linearForm}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a_1,dots,a_n$ be real numbers, and let
$xadicalc{-1,1}^n$. The centered square associated with $a$ and $x$ is
$(linearForm(a,x))^2-sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Linear form on a prefixed sign vector]
\lean{FABL.linearForm_fin_cons}
\label{FABL.linearForm_fin_cons}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.linearForm, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, sign
$b\in\{-1,1\}$, and vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the linear form satisfies
$L_a(b,x)=a_0b+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$, where $(b,x)$ denotes the vector obtained by
prefixing $b$ to $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment of a sign linear form]
\lean{FABL.expect_linearForm_sq}
\label{FABL.expect_linearForm_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_monomial_mul, FABL.linearForm, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $a=(a_i)_{i=0}^{n-1}$ be a real coefficient
vector. For a uniformly distributed point $x$ of the $n$-dimensional sign cube, the
expected square of the linear form $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} a_i x_i$ is $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}
a_i^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment of a sign decomposition]
\lean{FABL.expect_sq_eq_expect_odd_even}
\label{FABL.expect_sq_eq_expect_odd_even}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_fin_cons, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $d$ and $e$ be real-valued functions on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
$(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube. Suppose that for every sign $b$ and every point $x$ of
the $n$-dimensional cube, $f(b,x)=b\,d(x)+e(x)$. Then
$\mathbb{E}[f^2]=\mathbb{E}[d^2]+\mathbb{E}[e^2]$, where each expectation is uniform
over the cube on which its function is defined.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moment decomposition]
\lean{FABL.expect_fourth_eq_expect_odd_even}
\label{FABL.expect_fourth_eq_expect_odd_even}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_fin_cons, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $d,e:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ and $f:\\{-1,1\\}^{n+1}\\to\\mathbb R$. Suppose
that for every sign $b\\in\\{-1,1\\}$ and every $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$, adjoining $b$ as
the first coordinate gives $f(b,x)=b d(x)+e(x)$. Then $\\mathbb E[f^4]=\\mathbb
E[d^4]+6\\mathbb E[d^2e^2]+\\mathbb E[e^4]$, where each expectation is uniform over the
corresponding sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth-moment product inequality]
\lean{FABL.expect_sq_mul_sq_sq_le}
\label{FABL.expect_sq_mul_sq_sq_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $d$ and $e$ be any real-valued functions on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube. The square of the uniform expectation of $d(x)^2e(x)^2$ is at
most the product of the uniform expectations of $d(x)^4$ and $e(x)^4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of a squared-function expectation]
\lean{FABL.expect_sq_nonneg}
\label{FABL.expect_sq_nonneg}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be any real-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube. The uniform expectation of $f(x)^2$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of a fourth moment]
\lean{FABL.expect_fourth_nonneg}
\label{FABL.expect_fourth_nonneg}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real-valued function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, its uniform fourth
moment is nonnegative: $\\mathbb E[f^4]\\ge 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of a product of squares]
\lean{FABL.expect_sq_mul_sq_nonneg}
\label{FABL.expect_sq_mul_sq_nonneg}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $d$ and $e$ be any real-valued functions on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube. The uniform expectation of $d(x)^2e(x)^2$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $d,e:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and
$f:\{-1,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. Suppose that for every sign $b\in\{-1,1\}$ and every
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, $f(b,x)=bd(x)+e(x)$; suppose also that $\mathbb E[d^4]\le(\mathbb
E[d^2])^2$ and $\mathbb E[e^4]\le9(\mathbb E[e^2])^2$, with expectations uniform on the
respective cubes. Then $\mathbb E[f^4]\le9(\mathbb E[f^2])^2$, with expectation uniform
on the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $d,e:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and
$f:\{-1,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. Suppose that for every sign $b\in\{-1,1\}$ and every
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, $f(b,x)=bd(x)+e(x)$; also suppose that $\mathbb E[d^4]\le 9(\mathbb
E[d^2])^2$ and $\mathbb E[e^4]\le 81(\mathbb E[e^2])^2$, with expectations uniform on
the respective cubes. Then $\mathbb E[f^4]\le 81(\mathbb E[f^2])^2$, with expectation
uniform on the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moments of linear forms and centered squares]
\lean{FABL.linearForm_and_centeredSquare_fourthMoment}
\label{FABL.linearForm_and_centeredSquare_fourthMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.centeredLinearSquare, FABL.fourthMoment_le_eightyOne_of_slice, FABL.fourthMoment_le_nine_of_slice, FABL.linearForm, FABL.linearForm_fin_cons, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{6}
For every natural number $n$ and every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$, let $X$ be
uniformly distributed on $\{-1,1\}^n$ and let $L_a(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i$. Then
$\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^4]\le 9\bigl(\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^2]\bigr)^2$. Also, writing
$C_a(X)=L_a(X)^2-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2$, one has $\mathbb{E}[C_a(X)^4]\le
81\bigl(\mathbb{E}[C_a(X)^2]\bigr)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a$ be a real coefficient vector indexed by $n$
coordinates, and let $X$ be uniformly distributed on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube.
Define $Q(X)=(\sum_i a_i X_i)^2-\sum_i a_i^2$. Then $\mathbb E[Q(X)^4]\le
81\bigl(\mathbb E[Q(X)^2]\bigr)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For any real-valued function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and any point $x$ of
that cube, the degree-one part of the Fourier expansion of $f$ at $x$ equals the linear
form whose coefficient at coordinate $i$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ on the
singleton set $\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Centered square from first-level Fourier data]
\lean{FABL.centeredLinearSquare_singletonCoeffs}
\label{FABL.centeredLinearSquare_singletonCoeffs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.centeredLinearSquare, FABL.degreePart, FABL.degreePart_one_eq_linearForm, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_eq_sum_singleton}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
Boolean cube, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. Form the linear function whose
coefficient at coordinate $i$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the singleton set
$\{i\}$. Its centered square at $x$ equals the square of the degree-one part of $f$ at
$x$ minus the total squared Fourier weight at degree one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squared error after removing the linear part]
\lean{FABL.expect_sub_degreePart_one_sq}
\label{FABL.expect_sub_degreePart_one_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.degreePart, FABL.degreePart_one_eq_linearForm, FABL.expect_linearForm_sq, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_eq_sum_singleton, FABL.linearForm, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The uniform
expectation of the squared difference between $f$ and its degree-one Fourier part equals
the uniform second moment of $f$ minus its total Fourier weight at level one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squared error and level-one Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.expect_toReal_sub_degreePart_one_sq}
\label{FABL.expect_toReal_sub_degreePart_one_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.degreePart, FABL.expect_sub_degreePart_one_sq, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, viewed as a real-valued function. Write $\widehat
f(S)=\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$ for its Fourier coefficient at a coordinate
set $S$, and let $f_1(x)=\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be its degree-one
part. Then $\mathbb{E}_x[(f(x)-f_1(x))^2]=1-\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat f(S)^2$, where the
expectations are uniform on the sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment of the centered linear square]
\lean{FABL.expect_centeredLinearSquare_sq}
\label{FABL.expect_centeredLinearSquare_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.centeredLinearSquare, FABL.expect_linearForm_sq, FABL.linearForm, FABL.mean, FABL.variance, FABL.variance_linearForm_sq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}$. For a uniformly
chosen $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, set $L(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$. Then one half of the average
of $\left(L(x)^2-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2\right)^2$ equals $\left(\sum_{i=1}^n
a_i^2\right)^2-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^4$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\\{-1,1\\}$. The sum of the
squared Fourier coefficients of its real-valued sign representation over singleton
subsets lies in $[0,1]$.

\difficulty{4}
Let $s,t,\delta$ be real numbers such that $s^2=1$, $0\leq\delta\leq 1/1600$, and
$1521\delta<(t^2-1)^2$. Then
\[
169\delta\leq(s-t)^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound on a uniform probability]
\lean{FABL.one_div_144_le_uniformProbability_four_mul_sq_ge_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.one_div_144_le_uniformProbability_four_mul_sq_ge_secondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set and let $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. If the uniform
average of $g^2$ is positive and the uniform average of $g^4$ is at most $81$ times the
square of the uniform average of $g^2$, then the uniform probability of the set of
$x\in\Omega$ for which the uniform average of $g^2$ is at most $4g(x)^2$ is at least
$1/144$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Centered linear-square moment bound]
\lean{FABL.expect_centeredSingletonSquare_sq_le}
\label{FABL.expect_centeredSingletonSquare_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.centeredLinearSquare, FABL.centeredLinearSquare_fourthMoment_le, FABL.centeredLinearSquare_singletonCoeffs, FABL.degreePart, FABL.exercise9_5, FABL.expect_toReal_sub_degreePart_one_sq, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.one_div_144_le_uniformProbability_four_mul_sq_ge_secondMoment, FABL.sq_sub_one_far_of_centered_far, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f$ be a function from the sign cube
$\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{-1,1\\}$. For each subset $S\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, let
$\\widehat f(S)$ be its Fourier coefficient, and let $W_1(f)=\\sum_{|S|=1}\\widehat
f(S)^2$. If $0\\le\\delta\\le 1/1600$ and $W_1(f)=1-\\delta$, then, for a uniformly
random $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$, the expected square of $\\bigl(\\sum_{i=1}^n\\widehat
f(\\{i\\})x_i\\bigr)^2-\\sum_{i=1}^n\\widehat f(\\{i\\})^2$ is at most $6400\\delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth powers of singleton Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.one_sub_3202_mul_le_sum_singletonCoeff_fourth}
\label{FABL.one_sub_3202_mul_le_sum_singletonCoeff_fourth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.centeredLinearSquare, FABL.expect_centeredLinearSquare_sq, FABL.expect_centeredSingletonSquare_sq_le, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_eq_sum_singleton}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\\widehat
f(S)=\\mathbb E_x[f(x)\\prod_{j\\in S}x_j]$ denote its Fourier coefficient on the
uniform Boolean cube. If $0\\le\\delta\\le 1/1600$ and the total Fourier weight at level
$1$, namely $\\sum_{|S|=1}\\widehat f(S)^2$, equals $1-\\delta$, then
$1-3202\\delta\\le\\sum_{i=1}^n\\widehat f(\\{i\\})^4$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, where $n>0$, and let
$0\le\delta\le 1/1600$. If the total Fourier weight at level one of the real-valued
version of $f$ equals $1-\delta$, then some coordinate $i$ satisfies $1-3202\delta\le
\widehat f(\{i\})^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound on relative Hamming distance]
\lean{FABL.relativeHammingDist_le_one}
\label{FABL.relativeHammingDist_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\\beta$ be a set with decidable equality,
and let $f,g:\\Omega\\to\\beta$. Their relative Hamming distance is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of relative Hamming distance]
\lean{FABL.relativeHammingDist_nonneg}
\label{FABL.relativeHammingDist_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\\beta$ be a set with decidable equality,
and let $f,g:\\Omega\\to\\beta$. Their relative Hamming distance is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b002}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube. Suppose $0\leq\delta\leq 1/1600$ and the sum of the squared level-one Fourier
coefficients of the real-valued version of $f$ is $1-\delta$. Then some coordinate
dictator, or its negation, differs from $f$ on at most a fraction $1601\delta$ of the
inputs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Signed dictator function]
\lean{FABL.signedDictator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p044-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p129-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p138-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p252-b002
}
\label{FABL.signedDictator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.dictator}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate, and choose whether to negate the
output. The signed dictator function returns the sign at coordinate $i$, negated when
that choice is true.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function.
Suppose $0\leq\delta\leq 1/1600$ and the sum of the squares of the level-one Fourier
coefficients of $f$ is at least $1-\delta$. Then there is a coordinate $i$ and a choice
of sign such that the fraction of inputs on which $f$ differs from that signed
coordinate function is at most $1601\delta$.
\end{theorem}
